title: Takeout Opening Checklist
items:
> Position: Takeout Station
> Shift: Weekend / High Volume
# HEAT & EQUIPMENT (DO FIRST)
Burners on
Bains on and heating:  Alfredo  Marinara
Chaffer set with sauces
2 water pots filled and heating
Small pot + strainer set for GF
# MEATBALLS & PASTA
2 meatball pots started (meatballs + water)
Rigatoni (full pan) hung
Vermicelli (full pan) hung
4–6 strainer baskets set
Drip pot set under strainers
# PRODUCT PULL
> Freezer
Meat tortellini  Cheese tortellini  Meat ravioli  Cheese ravioli  Gnocchi
> Cooler (ON ICE)
Bolognese mix  Demi glaze  Chicken  Sausage  Shrimp
# PREP TABLE
Romano
Parsley
Oil (squeeze)
White wine (squeeze)
Butter (pats)
Salt/pepper
# STATION SETUP
Cutting board
Chef knife
Tongs (pasta)
Tongs (proteins)
Station organized for flow
# HOT CHECK
Alfredo hot
Marinara hot
Meatballs heating
Water near boil
# READY CHECK
Rig + verm stocked
2 meatball pots going
All proteins on ice
Sauces ready
Station clean
Tools set

title: Takeout Closing Checklist
items:
> Position: Takeout Station
> Shift: Dinner Close (Weekend / High Volume)
# PRECLOSE (WITH APPROVAL)
Check with chef/lead before starting
Confirm remaining volume
Confirm shutdown timing
# CONSOLIDATE
Combine Alfredo
Combine marinara
Consolidate proteins (keep on ice):  Chicken  Sausage  Shrimp  Bolognese  Demi
# REDUCE STATION
Reduce to minimum strainer baskets
Consolidate tools
Clear unused pans
# LIGHT CLEAN
Wipe surfaces
Clean/rotate cutting board
Remove trash buildup
Keep floor clean
# FINAL PUSH READY
Rig stocked
Verm stocked
Sauces sufficient
Proteins stocked
# CLOSE DOWN (AFTER LAST TICKET)
# SHUT OFF
Burners off
Remove water pots
Remove meatball pots
Remove strainers
# PRODUCT
Store or discard:  Sauces  Proteins  Pasta
Label and date
All TCS items to cooler immediately
# CLEAN EQUIPMENT
Clean burners
Clean bains
Clean chaffer
Wash:  Pots  Strainers  Utensils
# STATION
Empty ice pans
Clean cutting board
Clean knife
Sanitize all surfaces
# TRASH & FLOORS
Trash out
Sweep
Mop
# FINAL CHECK
Station is empty and clean
No food left out
Equipment off
Product stored properly
Check out with chef

title: Salad Closing Checklist
items:
# Pre-Close (Start When Volume Slows)
Check remaining tickets and expected volume
Begin consolidating product using FIFO
Combine like items into single containers
Restock anything needed to finish service cleanly
Ensure dressings (Italian, Ranch, Caesar) can carry through close
Set up backup containers for storage
Do NOT break down:
> Greens
> Tomatoes
> Core dressings
> Communicate with expo before removing any items
# Closing Checklist (After Last Ticket)
# Product Breakdown
Remove all items from cold rail
Inspect greens (discard any wilted product)
Discard unusable or expired items
Consolidate all usable product using FIFO
Transfer to proper storage containers
Wrap, label, and date all items
# Dressings
Consolidate soufflés where applicable
Store all dressings properly
Ensure minimal usable product remains for next shift
Wipe down all dressing containers
# Dry & Backup Items
Consolidate croutons (line + backup)
Seal all dry goods properly
Store in designated area
# Equipment & Station Breakdown
Remove and break down all cold rail pans
Send all utensils, pans, and containers to dish
Remove cutting boards
Clear entire work surface
# Cleaning
Clean inside cold rail (remove debris/liquid)
Wipe down all stainless surfaces
Sanitize cutting boards and station
Wipe down all containers and lids
# Floors & Trash
Sweep entire station (including under unit)
Mop floor
Empty trash
Replace liners
# Reset & Organization
Store all product in proper walk-in locations
Group items logically for next shift
Do NOT leave loose or unwrapped product
Do NOT leave unlabeled containers
# Final Check
Cold rail empty and clean
All product stored and labeled
No spoiled product left
Station fully wiped and sanitized
Floor clean and dry
Station set for next service
# Non-Negotiables
Do NOT leave bad greens for next shift
Do NOT leave station dirty “for morning”
Do NOT skip labeling
If it’s not clean, it’s not closed

title: Sauté Opening Checklist
items:
# Start-Up
Turn on sauté burners and set to low heat.
Turn on range hoods (MUA, fans, lights).
Check that all burners are functioning properly.
# Station Setup
Stock all sauces from prep:
Alfredo
Marinara
Seafood sauce
Stock dairy and liquids:
3 qt heavy cream
1 squeeze bottle oil
1 squeeze bottle white wine
1 squeeze bottle vodka
Stock fats:
1/9 pan Lamacha butter
1/6 pan butter
# Vegetables & Garnish
Stock:
1/6 pan broccoli
1/3 pan mixed vegetables
1/3 pan mushrooms
1/9 pan lemons
1 qt parsley
1/6 pan Romano cheese
1 qt microgreens
# Proteins & Seafood
Stock and rotate (FIFO):
1/3 pan chicken (chopped)
1/3 pan shrimp
1/6 pan clam meat
1/6 pan clams (shell)
1/6 pan mussels
2” half pan scallops (layered with towels)
# Pasta
Stock:
1/2 pan linguine
1/2 pan fettuccine
Confirm that backup pasta is available.
# Prep
Clarify butter and have it ready before service.
Check all seafood for quality and freshness.
Discard any unusable product.
# Mise en Place
Ensure all items are:
Stocked to PAR
Within arm’s reach
Properly organized
# Tools & Equipment
Set up:
Sauté pans
Tongs
Spoons
Towels
# Station Organization
Set clear work areas:
Cooking area
Ingredient area
Plating area
Ensure:
No clutter
Clean surfaces
Sanitizer and towels ready
# Communication
Confirm with:
Spoon station
Sauce jack
Verify:
Pasta availability
Sauce availability
Special items or tickets
# Quality Check
Test burner heat.
Taste sauces and adjust if needed.
Confirm that all proteins are ready.
# Final Check
Before first ticket:
Burners hot and ready
Station fully stocked
Seafood rotated and fresh
Butter clarified
Pasta stocked
Station clean and organized
# Standard
The station must be fully ready before the first ticket is printed.
No critical setup should happen during service.

title: Sauté Closing Checklist
items:
# Pre-Closing
Begin during slow periods while maintaining full-service capability.
Do not break down critical equipment before final push.
# Product Consolidation
Consolidate all seafood using FIFO:
Shrimp
Clams
Mussels
Scallops
Consolidate sauces and dairy into proper containers.
Discard any unusable or low-quality product.
# Pasta & Station Management
Reduce excess pasta on the line.
Ensure enough pasta remains for final tickets.
Cover and store pasta properly.
# Station Organization
Remove unused containers and tools.
Organize the station for closing.
Maintain clear working areas.
# Cleaning (Ongoing)
Wipe the surfaces between tickets.
Keep burners and pans clean.
Replace towels and sanitizer as needed.
# Communication
Notify chef of:
Low sauces
Low seafood
Low pasta
Any station issues
Communicate with spoon and sauce jack on remaining product.
# Closing
Confirm all tickets are complete before breakdown.
Communicate with expo and kitchen before shutting down.
# Equipment Shutdown
Turn off all burners.
Allow equipment to cool before cleaning.
# Product Breakdown & Storage
Store all sauces in clean containers (label and date).
Store seafood properly following food safety standards.
Store vegetables and garnishes properly.
Discard any unusable or contaminated product.
# Cleaning
Send to dish:
Sauté pans
Utensils
Containers
Clean:
Burners and stove top
Stainless surfaces
Backsplash and walls
Surrounding areas
# Floors & Trash
Remove all trash and replace liners.
Sweep floors thoroughly.
Mop floors.
# Restocking
Ensure basic station items are restocked for next shift.
Confirm sauces and key ingredients are ready.
# Final Check
Report to chef or manager:
Low inventory
Equipment issues
Product concerns
Confirm station is fully reset and ready.
# Notes
Maintain FIFO at all times.
Do not break down early and compromise service.
Closing is preparation for the next shift, not just cleanup.

Turn on holding wells

Ensure sauce is hot and service-ready
# Meatball Setup

Set up:
3 pots (weekday)
4 pots (weekend)
Begin heating meatballs
Ensure proper holding temperature
# Station Setup
Gather containers (quarts, pints, lids)
Gather utensils:
Ladles
Spoons
Tongs
Mixing tools
Set tools in consistent positions
Ensure station is clean and organized
# Pasta & Support Readiness

Be ready to:
Drop rigatoni when needed
Retrieve specialty pastas (WW, GF, pappardelle, etc.)
# Lasagna & Manicotti (If Applicable)
Confirm if pans are needed based on day/volume
Coordinate with hoagie bench
Set up chaffer pans if required
# Communication
Confirm readiness with:
Spoon station
Sauté station
Hoagie bench
Confirm expected volume and special items
# Final Check
Sauce hot and at proper consistency
Sauce jack filled appropriately for volume
Meatballs hot and stocked
Station clean and fully set

title: Sauce Jack Closing Checklist
items:
# Pre-Close
Begin reducing sauce based on volume
> 1 hour to close → 1/2 jack
> 30 minutes to close → 1/3 jack
Stir sauce regularly to maintain consistency
Consolidate meatballs using FIFO
Reduce number of pots as volume slows
Ensure enough meatballs remain for service
Monitor lasagna and manicotti pans (if active)
Count tickets before pulling replacement pans
Send unused utensils and excess pots to dish
Organize station and remove clutter
Wipe down sauce jack exterior and surrounding areas
Stock containers (quarts, pints, lids) for remaining service
Continue supporting sauté and spoon as needed
# Closing
# Service Completion
Confirm all tickets are complete with expo
# Equipment Shutdown
Turn off sauce jack
Turn off burners
Allow equipment to cool
# Product Breakdown
Remove remaining sauce from sauce jack
Transfer to clean containers
Label and date all sauce
Store properly
Discard unusable product
Consolidate meatballs
Store, cover, label, and date
Discard unusable product
Remove lasagna and manicotti pans
Cover and store or return to proper area
# Dish & Equipment
Sauce pots to dish
Meatball pots to dish
Utensils to dish
Break down and clean sauce jack
# Station Cleaning
Wipe and sanitize all surfaces
Clean burners and surrounding areas
Clean walls and backsplash
# Floors & Trash
Remove trash and replace liners
Sweep station area (including under equipment)
Mop floors with hot water and degreaser
# Final Steps
Restock containers and basic supplies
Report to chef:
Low sauce
Low meatballs
Equipment issues
Product concerns
Confirm station is clean and fully reset
# Standard
Station is fully ready for next service before leaving

title: Spoon Opening Checklist
items:
# Spoon Station
Turn on meatball pots and begin heating first as this is long cook for prep.
Turn on pasta burners.
Fill pasta pots and bring them to a full rolling boil.
Turn on the sauce jack and begin heating the meat sauce.
Turn on holding wells and bring to temperature.
Load meat sauce into sauce jack and stir regularly while heating.
Ensure sauce is hot, smooth, and at proper consistency before service.
Set up meatballs. 3 pots weekday, 4 pots weekend. Ensure proper hot holding temperature.
Confirm refill plans for meatballs. (plan head)
Pull all pasta and stock to PAR levels:
Rigatoni, spaghetti (vermicelli), whole wheat, gluten free, linguini, fettuccine, penne, pappardelle. (check levels)
Ensure all pasta bins are full, organized, and within arm’s reach.
Set backup pasta in reach for service.
Set up plating area with bowls/plates.
Set up ladles, spoons, and utensils for service
Organize station into working zones: pasta drop, sauce area, plating area.
Remove any clutter from the station.
Set towels and sanitizer bucket in proper place.
Communicate with expo, middle, sauté, and hoagie bench to confirm readiness.
Confirm sausage availability and any special item of coordination.
Test pasta drops to confirm the cook time.
Taste sauce and verify quality.
Verify that all hot items are at proper temperature.
Final check before service:
Pasta water at rolling boil.
Sauce hot and ready.
Meatballs are hot and stocked.
Pasta is fully stocked with PAR.
Station clean, organized, and ready.
No service begins until the station is fully set up.
If time permits, assist other stations or prep as needed.

> Notify closing chef of:

Middle
Sauté
Hoagie Bench

Remove all sauces from sauce jack

Discard unusable or contaminated product
> Dish & Equipment Cleaning
Pasta pots to dish
Meatball pots to dish
Strainers to dish
Ladles to dish
Utensils to dish
Steam table inserts to dish
Break down and clean sauce jack
> Station Cleaning
Wipe and sanitize all surfaces

Clean surrounding areas
> Floors & Trash

Replace trash liners

Equipment issues
Product concerns

title: Hoagie Bench Opening Checklist
items:
# Hoagie Bench
Turn on any lights that have not been turned on.
Turn on back ovens in prep area and takeout.
Turn on the top and bottom temps to 400 and turn on the top oven.
Turn on the hoagie bench cold rail.
Turn on flattop
Close drains on steam table and fill wells on both sides. Turn on low.
Turn on rangehoods flipping MUA and Fans on and the light as well.
Collect pans for cold rail and steam table. Also get tongs, spoons, and any other utensils needed for service.
Place pans into the wells of the steam table. 6-inch-deep half pans.
Pull out the product from the low boy in the hoagie station and place in cold rail. Fill in the empty spots with the pans you collected from dish.
Start bread. 22 minutes at 400 degrees for house loaves. Fill rack with 12 pans.
Check sheets for upcoming takeout and banquets, plan any needed items into the product you are panning.
Pull thawed lasagna and cut for pans and boats, referencing the par sheet.
Pull frozen lasagna to replace the ones you pulled to cut.
Make your Manicotti pans and boats referencing the par sheet
At approximately 10 am you should be putting the hoagie meat on the flattop. Cooking with butter and seasoning with salt/pepper and Montreal steak seasoning.
Last item, right before opening, cook to-go bread for 12 minutes at 400 degrees.
Double check to make sure you have panned enough product for the takeouts and banquets.
If time permits, assist the prep team with anything they may need help with.

title: Hoagie Bench Closing Checklist
items:
# Pre-Closing
Obtain Pans from the dish room to transfer cold rail product to new pans.
Take to dish any utensils and pans that are no longer needed for service.
Wipe down the front, sides, and top of the oven.
Arrange the oven screens by size (i.e. Small, Medium, and Large)
Stock the hoagie bench with pizza boxes, buns, pizza crusts, takeout boxes, etc.
Put water on to boil in the prep area for mop bucket
# Closing
Pull all pans from the cold rail and store in the low boy underneath the station.
Turn off the cold rail.
Turn off the steam table and drain it.
Turn the temperature of the top oven to 400 degrees and turn it off.
Turn down the bottom oven to 0 degrees but do not turn it off.
Turn off the back oven in prep area and the oven by takeout.
Clean the hoagie bench inside and out. Make sure to get all the debris out of the cold rail well.
Clean cutting boards
Wipe down the rest of the hoagie bench with stainless steel on the hoagie bench. Replace the cutting boards
Spray off the butter brushes and bring them back to the station. Do not give it to the dish crew.
Pull hoagie meat and meatballs and dispose of the product.
Wrap the butter and place it in the cooler.
Clean the flattop.
Remove and clean the flattop surround. Replace it back on the flattop.
Clean the steam table. This includes the shelf and the front of the table.
Finish wiping down the rest of the stainless steel.
Begin to sweep the line.
Put hot water in a mop bucket and fill the rest of the mop bucket with a degreaser cleaner from the mop sink room.
Mop the floor on the line and down both sides with the oven and sauce jack.
Notify the chef in charge of any low stock items.
Empty trash bins, put a bag back in it, and place it upside down on the line counters.
